I'm still working on trying to get this group engaged. Kylie had an art activity she needed to attend. Leo was in today, but did not come to tutoring. I was going to have them verbally tell me the the suffix and definition, but because we had so much time left over, I had them write it. We were in a classroom that was very loud. Scholars were distracted and it was sometimes difficult to hear. The schedule for this session is so short that there isn't really time to complete the lesson and the surveys. There is an IEP scholar in this session and is often disruptive.
This was a more dynamic lesson, with less tutor talk time. Somewhat better engagement.
This class is engaged and has a lot of energy. They fully participated in all activities.

Unfortunately, the classroom environment was quite loud, which made it difficult for our scholars to concentrate and fully benefit from tutoring. As Mr. Citro explained, until he receives approval from the superintendent, we are required to remain in the classroom rather than pull scholars out for tutoring. While we understand that we must follow these guidelines, the current arrangement limits our ability to provide the focused, individualized support these scholars need. Having access to a quieter setting or permission to work with scholars in a separate space would help us create a more productive learning environment and better support their academic progress.
This session was in a loud classroom. Very distracting to the students.

This group was receptive and engaged. They are friends and trust each other, so I felt confident in asking them to do the warmup, which asked them to move their bodies in silly ways to show the meaning of a word. They participated fully with all work on the BenQ board without prompting and completed all work.

This lesson went well. This is a group that works well together, and are open to trying new things. They participated in the human vocabulary machine warmup, which asks them to move in some silly ways.

This group has some students who don't want to be here and don't want to interact more than they have to. They complete the work, but they are not engaged. One seemed very slow to process information today.
I need to change things up a bit with this group. More interaction and multimodal expressions of knowledge.
Students enjoyed the lesson and were saying they hoped we could do more like it.

This group is very comfortable with each other, and conversation flows easily between them. They seemed relaxed in the room.

Thomas Oeter was pulled out of the classroom for speech. Students had a kinesthetic word warm up, then we talked about expectations, what we were going to be working on in our sessions, and an overview of the session structure.

Students were engaged throughout. We had a kinesthetic word warm up, then we discussed mutual expectations. I gave an overview of what we were going to be working on and what a typical session would look like. We discussed exit tickets. We ended with the survey.
